assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – assume ≥60 mL/min/1.73 m2; obtain baseline renal function before starting metformin and monitor thereafter.
Fasting lipid profile not available – order baseline lipids to confirm dyslipidaemia and to monitor ≥40 % non‑HDL‑C reduction after 3 months of statin.
QRISK score not calculated – assume ≥10 % based on age, hypertension, obesity, prediabetes, OSA; calculate at next visit to confirm statin indication.
Liver function tests not available – obtain baseline ALT/AST before initiating atorvastatin and repeat if clinically indicated.
Vitamin A, D, E, K supplementation required with Orlistat due to reduced fat‑soluble vitamin absorption.
Platelet MPV critically low – repeat full CBC to rule out hematologic disorder before any antiplatelet therapy.
Alcohol intake unknown – counsel patient to keep ≤14 units/week and document.
Smoking status unknown – assess and offer cessation support if applicable.
Thyroid function not assessed – consider TSH testing as hypothyroidism can contribute to dyslipidaemia and weight gain.
CPAP adherence for OSA not documented – review usage and optimise OSA management as it impacts BP and metabolic control.
treatment_summary: Start atorvastatin 20 mg nightly, metformin 500 mg BID (titrating as tolerated), and Orlistat 120 mg TDS with meals to address dyslipidaemia, prediabetes, and obesity respectively, while continuing lisinopril for hypertension and acetaminophen for pain. Baseline labs (renal function, liver enzymes, fasting lipids, CBC, TSH) and QRISK calculation are required before initiation. Monitor lipid profile at 3 months, HbA1c and renal function at 6‑12 months, and provide vitamin supplementation with Orlistat. Non‑pharmacological measures (diet, exercise, Diabetes Prevention Programme referral, OSA review) are also recommended.
